$comment: Publish footprint budget and build-mode rationale for the WPF desktop shell.
description: Documents the size/startup tradeoffs behind the WPF publish profile. This repository has no build CI: the local release build enforces this budget in Build-Scripts.ps1 -GenerateReleaseManifest, which fails past maxSizeMiB, warns past warnSizeMiB, and records the measured size in the release manifest under publishFootprint.

budget.rationale: The WPF shell ships as a compressed self-contained single-file executable. Compression measured 175.93 MiB down to 76.03 MiB on 2026-09-03, so 120 MiB leaves room for growth while keeping the download well inside typical browser and endpoint-tool limits.

buildModeDecisions.rationale: WPF trimming is not supported by Microsoft. The .NET trimmer cannot safely analyze WPF XAML bindings, resource dictionaries, or reflection-based converters. Enabling trimming produces runtime TypeLoadExceptions and missing-resource crashes in WPF apps. This decision should be revisited only if Microsoft announces official WPF trimming support.

ReadyToRun (R2R) pre-compiles IL to native code, improving cold-start time at the cost of larger binaries (typically 10-25% size increase). For LibreSpot, the startup cost is dominated by WPF framework initialization and the embedded PowerShell backend load, not JIT compilation. R2R would increase the artifact size without meaningfully improving perceived startup. This should be re-evaluated with measured before/after startup times if the executable approaches the budget ceiling.

Self-contained deployment avoids requiring users to install a specific .NET runtime. LibreSpot targets end users who may not have admin access or .NET knowledge. The size cost is significant but justified by the zero-prerequisite install experience.
Single-file bundling simplifies distribution: one file to download, verify, and run. The native extraction on first launch happens once per version.
Required for single-file to bundle native dependencies (e.g., WPF compositor, DirectWrite). Without this, the app would need a companion directory.

Measured on 2026-09-03 on this machine, three runs per variant, twice, using the offscreen --uia-smoke capture as the first-frame signal. Compression more than halves the download (175.93 MiB to 76.03 MiB) and makes the cold first launch faster, because the host reads far less from disk than it saves decompressing: cold 7023 ms and 5545 ms uncompressed against 5167 ms and 3771 ms compressed. Warm launches cost about 250 ms more (3643 ms and 3680 ms against 3898 ms and 3946 ms), which is inside the 1.5 s ceiling this decision was gated on.

coldStartMetrics.method: LibreSpot-Desktop.exe launched with --uia-smoke=recommended --uia-background --uia-size=1280x800 --uia-capture, timed from process start to the capture file appearing, with a fresh DOTNET_BUNDLE_EXTRACT_BASE_DIR per run so run 1 is a true cold start. Three runs per variant, repeated twice, on the maintainer machine.

measuredMetrics.description: Process start to the first offscreen frame, with no prior extraction.
Same measurement once the bundle has been extracted before.

coldStartMetrics.notes: First-refresh and working-set are still unmeasured: the offscreen capture completes before the environment snapshot finishes, so timing it needs a separate signal.
